title: Countries fall short on money to protect nature before big U.N. meeting
summary:
Nearly 200 countries promised to raise huge amounts of money to protect the world's oceans, forests, rivers and wildlife. So far, they have raised far less than they planned.

That gap will be a main topic at a United Nations meeting on biodiversity, called COP17, which begins Monday in Yerevan, Armenia, and is scheduled to end October 30. Biodiversity means the variety of plants and animals living on Earth. The countries will check their progress on 23 goals they agreed to in Montreal in 2022. The United States is not part of this treaty.

Under that deal, countries promised to raise $200 billion a year for nature by 2030. Data from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development shows they raised between $75 billion and $92 billion each year from 2023 to 2025, less than half the goal. A U.N. report released Thursday found that fewer than half of the targets are on track.

"We're not moving fast enough," said Astrid Schomaker, who leads the treaty's office.

One goal is going better. Countries were on track to give $20 billion a year to poorer countries by 2025, and $19 billion had been raised in 2024. However, a drop in foreign aid raises questions about whether that will continue.

There are other signs of progress. Countries have announced more than 5,000 projects connected to the treaty. The Philippines created an ocean area where catching rays and sharks is not allowed, and Argentina created a new national park in 2024. On Friday, a 17-nation group launched an effort to help threatened species recover. Nine private organizations also announced plans to spend $500 million over five years to prevent extinctions.
why_it_matters: Plants and animals support the food, water and air people rely on, so whether countries pay for protecting nature affects the whole planet's future.

keywords.explanation: Biodiversity is the variety of all the plants and animals living in a place or on Earth.
A treaty is a formal agreement between countries.
Targets are specific goals that people agree to try to reach.
Foreign aid is money or help that one country gives to another country.
Extinctions happen when a type of plant or animal dies out completely.
Threatened species are kinds of plants or animals at risk of disappearing.

background_read: Biodiversity is the variety of life on Earth, from tiny insects to huge forests, and healthy ecosystems give people food, clean water and air.
Many countries signed a United Nations treaty that commits them to protect nature, and they agreed on shared goals in Montreal in 2022.
The COP17 meeting is a regular gathering where these countries check how they are doing and decide what to do next.
Protecting land and oceans costs money for things like parks, scientists and rangers, which is why funding is a central issue.
